question: According to the Union Budget for 2025–26, presented in February 2025, approximately how much funding was allocated for pollution control in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹854 करोड़**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the Indian government allocated **₹854 करोड़** for pollution control initiatives, reflecting its commitment to combating environmental challenges.
 
• This allocation primarily targets measures to reduce **air, water, and soil pollution**, ensuring sustainable development and better public health outcomes.
 
• The fund will be utilized for projects such as **clean energy transitions**, promoting electric vehicles (EVs), and improving waste management systems.
 
• The allocation is part of India's broader strategy to meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement**, aiming for significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Special focus is given to urban areas with severe pollution levels, including cities listed under the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**

 
 
• Launched in **2019**, NCAP aims to reduce PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by **20-30%** by **2024** compared to 2017 levels.
 
• It focuses on 132 non-attainment cities identified by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**.
 
• Measures include strengthening air quality monitoring, promoting public awareness, and introducing pollution control technologies.
 
 
 
• **Electric Vehicle (EV) Promotion:**
 
 
• The government incentivizes the adoption of EVs through schemes like **FAME II** (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles).
 
• EV adoption reduces dependence on fossil fuels and minimizes **carbon emissions**.
 
 
 
• **Waste Management:**
 
 
• Initiatives like the **Swachh Bharat Mission** aim to improve solid waste management and reduce plastic pollution.
 
• The focus is on increasing the recycling of waste and promoting biodegradable alternatives to plastics.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement and India's Commitments:**
 
 
• India has pledged to reduce its **emissions intensity of GDP** by 33-35% by **2030** compared to 2005 levels.
 
• Efforts include increasing the share of renewable energy to **40% of installed capacity** by 2030.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Air Pollution in India:**

 
 
• India is home to several of the most polluted cities globally, with high levels of PM2.5 and PM10 particles.
 
• Major contributors include vehicular emissions, industrial activities, crop burning, and construction dust.
 
 
 
• **Government Laws and Guidelines:**
 
 
• The **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981** regulates air pollution control measures.
 
• The **Environment Protection Act, 1986** provides an overarching framework for pollution control in India.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• India's proactive measures, including solar energy adoption and pollution control funding, have been recognized internationally.
 
• Programs like **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** highlight India's leadership in renewable energy initiatives.
